title: Fleetwood stuns Arsenal, beats champions on penalties to reach Carabao Cup quarters
text:
Fleetwood stuns Arsenal, beats champions on penalties to reach Carabao Cup quarters - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 29일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Fleetwood stuns Arsenal, beats champions on penalties to reach Carabao Cup quarters 
 입력 2026.10.28. 18:21 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 A gap of as many as 84 places was closed. The 18th-place team in England's fourth tier toppled the defending Premier League champion. Fleetwood Town, based in a small coastal town, produced the greatest night in the club's history against Arsenal.
 BBC of the U.K. on the 28th (Korea time) highlighted the upset that shook English football, saying "Fleetwood Town beat Arsenal to advance to the Carabao Cup quarterfinals. It was the greatest night in the club's history."
 Fleetwood won on penalties after drawing 1-1 with Arsenal in the round of 16 of the 2026-2027 English Football League Cup (EFL Cup·Carabao Cup) held on the 27th.
 The objective difference in strength was hard to compare. Arsenal are the defending champions who topped the Premier League last season. By contrast, Fleetwood were sitting 18th in League Two, the fourth tier of English football. The difference in league positions between the two teams was as many as 84 places.
 Recent form also went against Fleetwood. Fleetwood had managed only one win in their last eight league matches. In the previous two games they lost 2-4 to Cheltenham Town and 1-2 to Exeter City. The defence, which had conceded six goals in those two games, raised doubts about whether it could stop the attacks of the Premier League champions.
 Once the match started, a flow different from expectations unfolded.
 Fleetwood took the lead in the 21st minute of the first half with a goal from Aaron Rupałović. Arsenal equalized in the second half with Viktor Gyokeres. Although Arsenal, the stronger side on paper, were expected to dominate the rest of the match, Fleetwood did not collapse easily.
 Instead, Arsenal faltered. After failing to properly capitalize on attacking opportunities, Max Dowman was sent off for kicking an opponent in reaction to a strong challenge from Harrison Neal.
 Fleetwood held out while enjoying a numerical advantage, and the match went to a penalty shootout.
 The player who decided the outcome was Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch. During the match he saved shots from Ben White and Martin Ødegaard to rescue his team from danger, and in the shootout he even stopped Bruno Guimarães's shot.
 When the final kicker, Connor Hogg, converted his penalty, Fleetwood's home ground, Highbury Stadium, erupted in ecstasy. Fans rushed onto the pitch and celebrated the historic victory with the players.
 Fleetwood manager Matt Roller, in an interview with Sky Sports after the match, said he was moved, saying "It is the greatest night in the club's history. Such an opponent came to our town, and we beat the champions."
 He added, "I really love football. I watch everything from the National League to the Premier League and the Championship. Even for me, this was a difficult match to prepare for. I'm pleased the players could feel these emotions. The players showed everything on the pitch and made this town, the club and everyone proud," he said.
 The players also could not hide their excitement at the unbelievable result.
 Left back Jake Batty reflected on BBC Radio 5 Live, saying, "Our league form hasn't been as good as we'd like. But strangely, when it comes to cup competitions something ignites in everyone's chest. Today had moments of magic."
 He then laughed, saying, "Isn't it a story to tell the grandchildren?"
 Batty said, "We are having a hard time. We are not a big club even in League Two. The fans who come to every game are just a few thousand. But you would have seen what the fans showed during the penalty shootout and throughout the match. The whole town is buzzing."
 He added, "This is exactly what we want to see on a Saturday in league matches. What if 5,000 fans came to support us every match? That support could give us momentum," he said.
 Fleetwood reached the League Cup quarterfinals for the first time since entering the English Football League in 2012.
 Batty emphasized, "It's unbelievable for this town. I hope we can play at home in the next round. And I want to do the same thing as today," adding, "I don't think there is a team we should fear."
 Fleetwood's victory prompted a look back at the club's history.
 Fleetwood is a club that, over the past 12 years, achieved promotion six times, rising from nonleague football to the English Football League. However, on April 20, 2024, relegation from League One was confirmed, and they dropped to the fourth tier.
 Coincidentally, on the same day Arsenal beat Wolverhampton Wanderers 2-0 to top the Premier League. Arsenal finished that season in second place and went on to win the Premier League two years later.
 The two clubs, which had walked in different directions, met in the League Cup in October 2026, and the smiling side was fourth-tier Fleetwood.
 Lynch, who made decisive saves in the penalty shootout, laughed, saying, "My voice was completely gone from shouting at the defense constantly."
 He said, "We took strength from Grimsby Town's win over Manchester United last season. We thought we could do something similar."
 He added emotionally, "It was a Fleetwood night. A storm was forecast and we knew the weather would not be good. I thought such conditions could work to our advantage. This victory is an incredible thing for the club and the entire town. It truly means everything to everyone."
 It was also a night fans will never forget.
 Ben, a fan who has supported Fleetwood for 15 years, told BBC Radio 5 Live, "I don't even remember my name right now. My phone won't stop ringing. I think I've received about 500 messages in the last 30 minutes."
 He said, "I went to the Exeter away game last weekend, and the previous Tuesday I went to the Cheltenham away game. In the Cheltenham match we were 0-3 down within 30 minutes of the start. Watching games like that makes me ask myself why I support this team."
 He added emotionally, "Today is not the best night of my football life. It is the best night of my entire life. I cannot put into words how happy and excited I am, how much this victory means to me. It is unbelievable that a club operating on such a small budget as ours has reached a moment like this."
 Despite the historic victory, reality awaits. Fleetwood must play a league match against Bristol Rovers on Saturday.
 Roller said, "It was really hard to know what to say to the players. I told them to enjoy today. And I told them we have a league match on Saturday."
 He added, "I didn't want to be the person to talk about reality, but we have a next match."
